reason: MSC.190(79) Annex 1 para 6.2.1 lists 'Off Smalls' verbatim (criterion 1, explicit naming). Closing line 21-22 confirmed in para 2.1: 52 10.3 N 006 21.8 W to 52 01.52 N 005 04.18 W. Named in para 6.2.1, so MRS only is supported. The partial-coverage arithmetic checks out. The 1996 centreline (COLREG.2/Circ.41, unchanged from A.284) is (1) 52 14.0 N 006 00.8 W, (2) 52 08.5 N 006 03.8 W, (3) 52 04.7 N 006 11.5 W. Line 21-22 lies at about 52 07.9 N at 006 00.8 W and 52 08.3 N at 006 03.8 W. Point 1 is therefore outside (Irish Sea side), point 3 is inside, and the line cuts the scheme near 52 08.2 N as the record says. Caveat for the record: 6.2.1 also lists 'Off Skerries', which lies wholly inside the Irish Sea beyond both closing lines. So the 6.2.1 list is not boundary-accurate, and the coordinates rather than the naming should govern the extent. Keep the partial note and flag this inconsistency in unresolved_issue. The Appendix 3 chartlet (dashed lines) was not visually checked.

Not named in the WETREP text, which is correct because the TSS was adopted in 2006. Coordinate check: COLREG.2/Circ.58 Annex 3 WGS 84 positions span about 57 23.7-57 29.0 N, 006 48.9-006 57.8 W. The WETREP outer boundary 62 N 003 W to 56 30 N 012 W crosses 57 26 N at about 010 29 W. The area runs from that line to the UK coast, with point 1 at 58 30 N on the UK coast and the only Irish Sea exclusions far to the south. The TSS is therefore about 3.5 degrees of longitude inside, satisfying criterion 2/3 (boundary demonstrably includes the TSS). Minor caveat: the Minches are UK internal waters. WETREP's coast-based definition does not exclude them, but this could be noted. MRS only stands.

All quotes confirmed. MSC.162(78) replacement para 2.1 sets the western limit at 010 15 W and states 'This area includes the traffic separation scheme Off Finisterre and the associated inshore traffic zones adopted by resolution A.767(18), as amended by resolution A.957(23)'. MSC.63(67) Annex 3 paras 3.3-3.4 make Finisterre VTS the shore authority, and para 7.1 describes its radar monitoring. MSC.190(79) 6.2.1 and 6.2.6 name Off Finisterre and Finisterre VTS, and the TSS lies inside the WETREP outer line (about 012 W at 43 N). For current operation, the Ministry's Tramos (February 2025, text by Salvamento Maritimo) says the DST are controlled by VTS, a function assigned to Salvamento Maritimo, including Fisterra. The Salvamento Maritimo site is still unreachable (TLS error by curl, HTTP 503 by WebFetch), so there is no operator-page confirmation. Note: the VTS area is evidenced only through FINREP plus the Tramos statement, not a separate VTS boundary instrument; this is acceptable under criteria 1 and 4.
